title: Regression impact notice and choice card
body:
TL;DR:
We observed a regression after the 2029-04-21 model rollout affecting structured-output and some completion consistency for a subset of requests. Impact window: 2029-04-21 04:12 UTC -> 2029-04-22 09:40 UTC. Material effect: higher incidence of truncated JSON-like responses and occasional hallucinated numeric fields for long prompts.

Who was affected:
- ~0.6% of production requests overall; skewed to tenants using structured-output and long-context routes (>2k tokens).
- Primary symptoms reported by integrators: malformed JSON, missing keys, and value drift for numeric identifiers.

Short root-cause summary (customer-facing):
- During a model variant rollout, a tokenization/serialization alignment in the model's training artifact changed how certain delimiter tokens are represented, which increased the likelihood of the model emitting truncated or malformed structured output under long-context conditions. The serving runtime and parser assumed the previous delimiter behavior, so the combination produced incomplete serialized outputs. This is not a data breach and no customer data was exfiltrated.

What we fixed so far:
1) Immediate mitigation: rolled back the model to the prior stable variant for all routed production traffic at 2029-04-22 09:40 UTC.
2) Hotfix: deployed a conservative structured-output post-processor that validates JSON-like outputs and triggers a safe retry path; active since 2029-04-22 11:05 UTC.
3) Telemetry: added a targeted metric (structured_output_validation_fail_rate) and a rapid alert to SRE and Product-MLOps.

Customer options and choice card (what you can choose now):
Option A — Stay on rolled-back variant (recommended for critical structured-output flows):
  - Effect: immediate return to pre-incident behavior, no code changes required on your side.
  - Action: no action needed; default for all customers after rollback.

Option B — Pin to prior stable variant for specific routes only:
  - Effect: leaves non-critical routes able to test newer variants while preserving structured-output routes on stable variant.
  - Action: open a ticket to request per-route pinning; include route IDs and expected traffic windows.

Option C — Opt into experimental replay + verification package (for customers who want regression evidence for compliance or QA):
  - Effect: we will re-run impacted requests against both the rolled-back and released variants in a replay environment and deliver a signed evidence bundle.
  - Action: opt-in via the support link; expected delivery 3–5 business days.

Option D — Accept controlled canary on your tenant (if you want to test latest variant with safety hooks):
  - Effect: we enable the new variant for a small percentage of your traffic with extra post-processing and human-in-the-loop checks.
  - Action: request via your AM or support; we will schedule a call to set thresholds.

Verification steps we recommend you run locally (quick checklist):
1) Re-run a representative prompt set (10–50 examples) that exercises long-context structured-output.
2) Validate returned payloads with a strict JSON schema; record failure rates.
3) If you see >0.5% schema failures, request per-route pinning and the replay package.

Evidence package contents (what we will provide if you opt-in):
- Replay logs: original request timestamps, original outputs, replayed outputs against both variants.
- Validation report: failure counts, sample diffs for failed messages, and a short explanation of likely failure mode per sample.
- Signed statement: incident timeline and mitigation actions by Redwood.

SLA and credits:
- This event meets the criteria for an SLA review. If your tenant experienced measurable impact (we define as failed structured-output >1% during the impact window), you will be eligible for a pro-rated credit. To start an SLA claim, open a ticket and include an example sample and route ID.

Timeline (customer-facing):
- 2029-04-21 04:12 UTC: new model variant began staged rollout.
- 2029-04-21 07:40 UTC: first automated spike detected in structured_output_validation_fail_rate; triaged by SRE.
- 2029-04-21 12:30 UTC: product + MLOps alerted; initial hypothesis logged.
- 2029-04-22 09:40 UTC: model rollback to stable variant executed.
- 2029-04-22 11:05 UTC: safe post-processor and retry path deployed.
- 2029-04-24 15:00 UTC: telemetry shows structured_output_validation_fail_rate back to baseline for all monitored tenants.

How to request actions from Redwood (practical steps):
- For per-route pinning: open support ticket with subject "Pin route to stable: <tenant-id> <route-id>". Include expected UTC windows if temporary.
- For replay/evidence package: open support ticket with subject "Replay request: INC-4532 evidence for <tenant-id>".
- For SLA credit: open support ticket with subject "SLA claim: regression impact INC-4532" and attach sample IDs.

Communication cadence going forward:
- Short follow-up note (this doc) will be posted to the status page within 24 hours summarizing rollback and verification state.
- A customer-facing postmortem with a deeper technical appendix and remediation plan will be shared within 10 business days.
- If you have regulatory/compliance needs requiring faster deliverables, flag that in the support ticket and we will prioritize evidence delivery.

Safety and data privacy note:
- No exfiltration or unauthorized access was detected. Replays are performed in an isolated environment; we will follow your tenant retention and data handling settings.

Contact points for immediate assistance:
- Primary: customer-success@redwood.ai (support portal link in the status page)
- Escalation (for enterprise customers): your assigned AM or account_ops@redwood.ai

Internal actions we are taking (brief, high level):
- Deep root-cause review between Serving Runtime, MLOps, and Model QA teams to prevent tokenization-serialization mismatch classes of regressions.
- Deployment gating improvements: we will expand pre-rollout validation to include structured-output stress tests at longer contexts.
- Post-deploy canary hygiene: add synthetic golden inputs and stricter rollback automation when structured_output_validation_fail_rate spikes.

Appendix A — Example request/response pair (redacted):
- Prompt: (redacted) long-context with JSON schema request
- Output (bad variant): "{\"items\": [{\"id\": 12345, \"amount\": 99.}"  <-- truncated and missing key
- Output (stable): "{\"items\": [{\"id\": 12345, \"amount\": 99.00, \"currency\": \"USD\"}]}"

Appendix B — Quick FAQ for customers:
Q: Was customer data exposed?
A: No. This was a model-output formatting regression and not an access control event.

Q: Will you prevent this from happening again?
A: We are instituting additional validation and gating checks specific to structured outputs and long-context scenarios.

Q: How long to get the replay package?
A: Expect 3–5 business days after opt-in; shorter for enterprise escalations.

Next steps for you (recommended):
1) If your product depends on strict structured-output, confirm per-route pinning now by opening a support ticket.
2) If you need an evidence package, opt-in.
3) Monitor the status page for the formal postmortem link in ~10 business days.

Prepared by: Customer Success (Aisha Patel), in coordination with Product-MLOps and SRE.

Draft notes (internal):
- Keep language non-technical in public status page; include the appendix as an optional download for customers who request deeper detail.
- Ensure legal reviews the evidence package template for regulated tenants.
